key_insight: Factual recall in LLMs follows a sigmoid function of a log-linear combination of model size (parameter count) and topic representation in the training data; those two factors alone explain ~60% of recall variance across evaluated dense models.
problem_solved: Provides the first empirical scaling relationship linking factual recall to both model scale and training-data composition, enabling prediction of when models will confidently (but not always correctly) produce references.
method: Evaluated 38 models on >8,900 scholarly references using an automated reference-verification pipeline to measure recall quality.
Quantified topic representation in training data and combined it with model parameter count in a log-linear predictor, then mapped predictor outputs to recall probability with a sigmoid fit.
Performed statistical analysis across 16 dense models from four model families to measure explanatory power (≈60% variance explained) of the two-factor model.
impact: Gives practitioners a simple, actionable rule-of-thumb to anticipate and improve factual recall by balancing model scale and dataset topic coverage—informing model selection, dataset curation, and risk assessment for hallucinated references.
visual_elements: 2D scatterplot of models (x: log(model params), y: topic frequency) with a fitted sigmoid surface/contour showing recall probability
Heatmap showing recall rate as a function of model size and topic representation, emphasizing the sigmoid transition region
Bar or pie chart reporting variance explained (R² ≈ 0.60) by the two-factor model versus alternative predictors
Icon set: model (chip), dataset (stacked documents), verification/checklist to visually link components of the method
paper_title: Predictable Confabulations: Factual Recall by LLMs Scales with Model Size and Topic Frequency
paper_authors: Matthew L. Smith, Jonathan P. Shock, Samuel T. Segun, Iyiola E. Olatunji, Tegawendé F. Bissyandé
